newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Madrid summit agreement worked out between Greece and Turkey has drawn fire from within ruling party PASOK and the government but praise from opposition figures, such as former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis. The agreement will probably be brought up for discussion at tomorrow's Cabinet meeting.

--United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan was positive about progress in the Cyprus issue, at the opening of talks under his auspices near New York yesterday. But US presidential emissary Richard Holbrooke warned that the recent Greek-Turkish agreement did not necessarily mean success at the talks.
--Opposition parties greeted developments in Greek-Turkish relations with "optimistic reservations", but ruling PASOK MPs are reportedly preparing their own response to the surprise agreement.
--Fires continued to take their toll of Greek forests, with 25,000 stremmata scorched in one regional fire.
--Doctors at public hospitals decided yesterday to continue their strike for yet another week, while pharmacies begin their six-day strike today.

--Turkish President Suleyman Demirel wants talks on the gamut of issues affecting bilateral relations with Greece, according to reports. The issues include economic cooperation, the battle against the illegal drug trade and illegal immigration.

--An experts' inquiry into the death of a young conscript at an Evros army camp two weeks ago has said his death was due to natural causes, rejecting claims by two coroners that the soldier was killed.
--Some 15-20 PASOK MPs have signed a letter opposing the Greek-Turkish agreement signed during the Madrid NATO summit and more are expected to add their dissent.

--The legendary Brigitte Bardot visited Greece yesterday to accept an award for her work protecting animals and the environment, and overcoming her vow to never visit Greece because it "tortured" its animals.
